newsitem.title: ITALY: Dolce & Gabbana let loose leopardskin collection.
newsitem.headline: Dolce & Gabbana let loose leopardskin collection.

text.p: Feline glamour slunk stealthily down the catwalk at the Milan fashion shows on Wednesday when Italian design duo Dolce & Gabbana let loose a leopardskin collection.

Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana, in a hall covered from ceiling to floor by leopardskin print, exploited length and lightweight transparent materials to give a willowy, flowing profile to their 1997 spring/summer women's collection.
With animal prints and trains trailing dramatically behind, the collection had a 1920s Bohemian air with large flowered motifs and dresses falling straight to the ankle.
The romantic impression deepened with models' hair scraped back under circlets and adorned at one side by bright flowers.

Satiny and gauzy housecoats featured with lapels cut wide open, buttoned just below the breast and flapping free to mid-calf, while a cream fur stole and coats with broad furred collars enriched the glamour.
Shoes were high-heeled wedge sandals with part of the wedge carved away while monochrome crocheted dresses and accompanying coats to mid-calf and ankle gave an elegant, elongated profile.
Dolce & Gabbana also set oriental prints on richly coloured straight satiny skirts and tunics as well as deep-dyed flower and leaf motifs on cream satin backgrounds.

They wound the display up with a litter of see-through slip dresses of varying lengths in monochrome creams, apricots and pale blues, some with trains floating behind and worn over leopardskin tap shorts.

Diminutive designer Anna Molinari also infused some smokey glamour into a collection of chiffon, lace, drop-waists and cutaway hemlines, adorning models with 1920s style feather headdresses and plenty of bangles and beads.
Glamour came too in the form of a cream flared summer coat with a wide-shouldered, rounded collar, reaching to mid-thigh and worn over a fuchsia slip dress.
Molinari used more obvious opulence with shiny gold tops over white cotton skirts and pants, as if asking rhetorically "Why should gold seem trite and used up?"
Following this season's fascination with things transparent, Molinari took plain white petticoats and placed lurex lace over the top, while shoes were backless with spindly medium-height heels.
Designer Krizia was to unveil her collection later on Wednesday while fashion house Gucci and designer Gianfranco Ferre parade theirs on Thursday and Friday.
Style king Gianni Versace presents his main collection on Saturday and Giorgio Armani closes the shows with his top line Giorgio Armani label on Sunday.
